Rashi on Keritot 19a:10:1.hebrew: ונעלם כו' - מדאפיק הני תרי ונעלם להך דרשא, אלמא לית ליה ידיעה בתחלה, דידיעת טומאה דבעי בתחלה ובסוף לא מפקא אלא מהנך תרי ונעלם, כדאמרן בפ"ק דשבועות (דף ד.):
Rashi on Keritot 19a:10:1.english: And it was concealed, etc. - Since he [Rabbi Yishmael] uses these two [mentions of] "and it was concealed" for this exposition, evidently he does not hold [that there is a requirement of] awareness at the outset; for the awareness of impurity that is required at the outset and at the end is derived only from those two [mentions of] "and it was concealed," as we stated in the first chapter of Shevuot (4a).

Rashi on Keritot 19a:12:1.english: Forbidden fat and notar [were] before him - And he thought both of them [were] permitted fat.

Rashi on Keritot 19a:12:2.hebrew: אשתו נדה ואחותו עמו בבית - בא על האחת, כסבור זו אשתו וכסבור שטהורה היא, ונמצא שאשתו היתה נדה, ועוד ספק על איזו מהן בא:
Rashi on Keritot 19a:12:2.english: His menstruating wife and his sister [were] with him in the house - He had intercourse with one [of them], thinking, "This is my wife," and thinking that she was pure; and it turned out that his wife was a menstruant, and furthermore, [it is] uncertain which of them he had intercourse with.

Rashi on Keritot 19a:12:3.hebrew: ור' יהושע פוטר - מפרש בגמרא: "אשר חטא בה", עד שיודע לו במה חטא:
Rashi on Keritot 19a:12:3.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua deems [him] exempt - [It is] explained in the Gemara: "[wherein] he has sinned" — until it becomes known to him in what [matter] he sinned.

Rashi on Keritot 19a:14:1.hebrew: או שעשה - מלאכה בשבת, ואינו יודע איזו מלאכה עשה, אם חרש אם זרע:
Rashi on Keritot 19a:14:1.english: Or one who performed - [a] labor on Shabbat, and he does not know which labor he performed, whether he plowed [or] whether he sowed.

Rashi on Keritot 19a:14:2.english: Even from a provisional guilt offering - [It] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Keritot 19a:15:1.hebrew: לא נחלקו - ר' אליעזר דאמר לא בעינן שידע במה חטא, [ור' יהושע דאמר בעינן שידע במאי חטא]:
Rashi on Keritot 19a:15:1.english: They did not disagree - Rabbi Eliezer, who says we do not require that he know with what he sinned, [and Rabbi Yehoshua, who says we require that he know with what he sinned].

Rashi on Keritot 19a:15:2.hebrew: על דבר שהוא משם אחד - כגון שתי אילנות של מין אחד לפניו, ולא ידע אם מזה לקט אם מזה:
Rashi on Keritot 19a:15:2.english: With regard to a matter that is from one category - For example, [when] two trees of one species [are] before him, and he does not know whether he picked from this [one] or from that [one].

Rashi on Keritot 19a:1:1.hebrew: רבי שמעון פוטר בזו - דשני טומאות נינהו, אכל חדא וחדא כניסה איכא למימר שביל זה הוא הטהור, והילכך ליכא ידיעה ודאית בתחלה, ובטומאת מקדש בעינן ידיעה בתחלה ובסוף והעלם בנתים. ות"ק דמחייב, מפרש טעמיה לקמן:
Rashi on Keritot 19a:1:1.english: Rabbi Shimon exempts [him] in this [case] - For they are two [separate] impurities; regarding each and every entry, one can say [that] this path is the pure one, and therefore there is no definite knowledge at the beginning, and in [cases of] impurity of the Temple, we require knowledge at the beginning and at the end, and unawareness in between. And [as for] the Tanna Kamma who holds [him] liable, [the Gemara] explains his reason below.

Rashi on Keritot 19a:2:1.hebrew: ואפילו בקמייתא - בתרתי קמייתא, בתמיה? והא איכא ידיעה ודאית בכניסה אחריתי:
Rashi on Keritot 19a:2:1.english: And even in the first [cases] - In the first two [cases], [asked] in astonishment: for is there not definite knowledge upon the second entry?

Rashi on Keritot 19a:2:2.hebrew: שכח שהלך בראשון - ואף על גב דטומאה ודאית היא, מיהא ליכא אלא מקצת הידיעה, דשכח את הראשון, ובהא פליגי הני תרי תנאי אליבא דר' שמעון. ת"ק אליבא דר' שמעון לא פטרו אלא בבתרייתא, דאילו בקמייתא, כיון דממה נפשך איכא טומאה, ידיעה ודאית שהלך בשניהם, אף על פי ששכח שהלך בראשון, אפילו הכי מקצת ידיעה כידיעה, והוה ליה ידיעה בתחלה; אבל בבתרייתא ליכא ידיעה ודאית:
Rashi on Keritot 19a:2:2.english: He forgot that he walked on the first - Even though it is definite impurity, nevertheless there is only partial knowledge, since he forgot the first [path]; and regarding this these two Tannaim disagree according to Rabbi Shimon. The first Tanna according to Rabbi Shimon only exempts him in the latter [case], whereas in the first [case], since either way there is impurity — [and] definite knowledge that he walked on both of them — even though he forgot that he walked on the first [path], even so partial knowledge is like [full] knowledge, and he has knowledge at the beginning; however, in the latter [case] there is no definite knowledge.

Rashi on Keritot 19a:2:3.hebrew: ור' שמעון בן יהודה סבר - אף על גב דטומאת ידיעה ודאית היא, כיון דליכא אלא מקצת ידיעה, כמאן דליתיה דמיא:
Rashi on Keritot 19a:2:3.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda holds - Even though it is [a case of] impurity of definite knowledge, since there is only partial knowledge, it is considered as if it does not exist.

Rashi on Keritot 19a:4:1.hebrew: ר' ישמעאל כו' - בפרק שני דשבועות (דף יד:):
Rashi on Keritot 19a:4:1.english: Rabbi Yishmael, etc. - In the second chapter of Shevuot (14b).

Rashi on Keritot 19a:6:1.english: And [the statement] of Reish Lakish is difficult [compared] to [that] of Reish Lakish - For why did he not establish it in accordance with Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], and say [that] uncertain knowledge [is] like certain [knowledge]?

Rashi on Keritot 19a:8:1.hebrew: ונעלם והוא טמא - משמע אף על גב דאיכא קצת העלמה בטומאה, חייב:
Rashi on Keritot 19a:8:1.english: And it was concealed... that he is impure - [This] implies [that] even though there is some concealment regarding the impurity, he is obligated [to bring an offering].

Tosafot on Keritot 19a:10:1.hebrew: הא מתניתין היא דתנן כו' - והקשה הרב ר' שמואל מווארדו"ן: והיכי מוכח מהאי מתניתין דמייתי דרבי ישמעאל לא בעי ידיעה בתחלה? לעולם אימא לך דבעי! אי משום דמפיק "ונעלם" "ונעלם" לדרשא אחריתי, הא חזינן רבי דסבר ידיעת בית רבו שמה ידיעה, ובעי ידיעת בית רבו אע"ג דמפיק "ונעלם" "ונעלם" להעלם טומאה ולהעלם מקדש כמו הכא, ומכל מקום בעי ידיעת בית רבו ממשמעות "ונעלם" — מכלל שידע כבר! ויש לומר: בשלמא רבי — אשכחנא בעלמא דבעי ידיעת בית רבו, א"כ גבי מקדש וטומאה נמי בעי לה; אבל רבי ישמעאל — לא אשכחנא בשום דוכתא דבעי ידיעת בית רבו. ועוד יש לומר: א"כ הוה ליה למימר בהדיא "ונעלם" — מכלל שידע כבר:
Tosafot on Keritot 19a:10:1.english: "But this is [already taught in] a mishna, as we learned," etc. - And Rabbi Shmuel of Verdun raised a difficulty: How is it proven from this mishna that [the Gemara] cites that Rabbi Yishmael does not require knowledge at the outset? Actually, I could say to you that he does require [it]! If [the proof is] because he expounds "and it was concealed" [and] "and it was concealed" for another exposition — behold, we see [that] Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] holds [that] knowledge [acquired in] his teacher's house is considered knowledge, and he requires knowledge [acquired in] his teacher's house even though he expounds "and it was concealed" [and] "and it was concealed" for a lapse of awareness of impurity and for a lapse of awareness of the Temple, just like here [with Rabbi Yishmael], and nevertheless he requires knowledge [acquired in] his teacher's house from the implication of "and it was concealed" — implying that he already knew [beforehand]! And one can answer: Granted [regarding] Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], we find elsewhere that he requires knowledge [acquired in] his teacher's house, [so] if so, regarding the Temple and impurity as well he requires it; however, [regarding] Rabbi Yishmael, we do not find anywhere that he requires knowledge [acquired in] his teacher's house. And furthermore, one can answer: If so, he should have stated explicitly: "And it was concealed" — implying that he already knew [beforehand].

Tosafot on Keritot 19a:9:1.hebrew: אדמוקמת כרבי ישמעאל לוקמה כרבי - וצ"ל על כרחך דלאו כרבי ממש, דאם כן, בלא קשיא דריש לקיש אדר"ל מצי למפרך: לוקמה כרבי ומטעם ידיעת בית רבו, ומש"ה חייב, דהוה ליה ידיעת בית רבו ורבי סבר שמה ידיעה. אלא הכי פריך: אדמוקמת ליה כרבי ישמעאל ומוקמת ליה בלא ידיעה כלל, לוקמה כרבי ובידיעת מקצת, כמו ידיעת ספק, דסבר רבי שמה ידיעה:
Tosafot on Keritot 19a:9:1.english: "Instead of your establishing [it] in accordance with Rabbi Yishmael, let him establish it in accordance with Rabbi" - And one must say perforce that [it is] not literally in accordance with Rabbi, for if so, [even] without the contradiction of Reish Lakish against Reish Lakish, one could ask: Let him establish it in accordance with Rabbi and for the reason of knowledge of his teacher's house [i.e., general knowledge learned in school], and for that reason he is liable, since he had knowledge of his teacher's house and Rabbi holds [that] it is considered knowledge. Rather, this is what it is asking: Instead of your establishing it in accordance with Rabbi Yishmael and establishing it without any knowledge at all, let him establish it in accordance with Rabbi and with partial knowledge, like doubtful knowledge, which Rabbi holds is considered knowledge.
